clue.text: Unassuming Burgundy perhaps for the lady?

parts.note: an unassuming manner is mild, gentle and modest
Burgundy is a wine that is often red, so it stands for the colour

explanation.surface: A wine waiter suggests a modest Burgundy as the right choice for a female diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burgundy perhaps' looks like the wine itself but only supplies its colour; 'the lady' is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildred is a traditional female first name, so it identifies a particular woman.

clue.text: This month incorporated opening of the faculty

parts.note: INST, short for instant, is old business shorthand for this month

indicators.note: opening of asks for the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A company was incorporated this month in time for a university faculty's opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faculty' looks like a university department but means an innate ability.
explanation.definitionFit: An instinct is an inborn ability or capacity, which is one sense of faculty.

clue.text: Former spirit's underlying Germany's stagnation

indicators.note: in a down answer, underlying means placed below the earlier piece

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
old means former
rum is a spirit; the 's adds S

explanation.surface: An old drink forming the basis of Germany's economic stagnation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'underlying' puts OLD RUMS below D.
explanation.definitionFit: In the doldrums means in a state of inactivity or slump, a stagnation.

clue.text: True alarm spreading about unknown non-resident

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other
spreading means the letters scatter into a new order

parts.note: X is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Real alarm grows about a stranger who does not live here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreading' rearranges TRUE ALARM, which goes 'about' X.
explanation.definitionFit: Extramural means outside the walls of an institution, as with students who do not live in.

clue.text: In discussion solitary makes advance

indicators.note: in discussion means as spoken aloud, so the word heard matters, not its spelling

parts.note: solitary means lone

explanation.surface: A lone person speaking up makes progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advance' looks like progress but means money lent.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance is money paid ahead, effectively a loan.

clue.text: Design from bone set in flexible mica

indicators.note: set in means the piece is placed inside the other
flexible suggests letters that bend into a new shape

parts.note: OS is the Latin word for bone

explanation.surface: A design made from bone inlaid in pliable mica.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flexible' rearranges MICA; OS goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mosaic is a decorative picture or pattern made of small pieces.

clue.text: Fish product that's substandard turned up containing still more in the middle

indicators.note: containing means the first piece holds the second
in a down answer turned up means read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: substandard means poor

indicators.note: in the middle takes the central letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A shoddy fish product turns out to have even more stuffed inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses POOR to ROOP; 'in the middle' takes LLM from 'still more'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a rolled pickled herring fillet, a prepared fish dish.

clue.text: My sonny — this needs rewriting — word for word!

indicators.note: needs rewriting means the letters have to be written out again differently

explanation.surface: A parent's note that their son's essay must be redone in full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'word for word' looks like 'verbatim' but means a word replacing another word.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym is a word that can stand in for another word with the same meaning.

clue.text: Dullness unacceptable between physician and his number three

indicators.note: between says one piece sits in the gap separating two others

parts.note: MO is short for Medical Officer, an army doctor
his refers back to the physician, whose third letter is Y
something unacceptable is 'not on' in British idiom

explanation.surface: A tedious tale of a doctor and his third wife behaving badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his number three' looks like a third spouse but means the third letter of 'physician'. NOT ON is British slang for unacceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotony is tedious sameness, a direct synonym of dullness.

clue.text: One well overdue to be cut off

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
'well' and 'so' both serve as a hesitating start to a sentence
something overdue is late

explanation.surface: A single well that has not been serviced in time faces being disconnected.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate something is to separate it so it is cut off from everything else.

clue.text: Giant oil reproduced in engraving

indicators.note: reproduced suggests the letters are produced again in a new order

explanation.surface: A huge oil painting has been copied as an engraving.
explanation.definitionFit: An intaglio is a design cut into a surface, a form of engraving or incised gem.

clue.text: It's awkward when Clinton's off his head and a bother

indicators.note: off his head means the man loses his first letter

parts.note: Bill Clinton was the US President
to tease is to pester or bother

explanation.surface: Things are awkward when Bill Clinton is losing his mind and causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off his head' looks like madness but takes B from BILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill at ease describes someone uncomfortable or embarrassed, feeling awkward.

clue.text: Vehicle's range?

definitions.meaning: the Ford ... was a popular family car

explanation.surface: How far can this car travel on one tank?
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like a car's driving distance but is a chain of mountains; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ford named a model the Sierra, and sierra is Spanish for a toothed mountain chain.

clue.text: Presenter nearly beside Ms Giedroyc lay vacuously down

indicators.note: beside puts the first piece next to what follows

parts.note: Mel Giedroyc is a British TV presenter, once a host of The Great British Bake Off

indicators.note: nearly means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: a news presenter is an anchor

indicators.note: vacuously means emptied, so only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A TV presenter lies idly next to Mel Giedroyc, feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: Mel Giedroyc co-presented The Great British Bake Off. 'nearly' cuts ANCHOR to ANCHO; 'vacuously' empties LAY to LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down and feeling melancholy are both ways of being sad or dejected.

clue.text: Turning over in bed to see workers in the dark?

definitions.text: Turning over in bed to see workers in the dark?

parts.words: Turning over in bed to see workers in the dark?
parts.note: a shift is a turning over, and the night is when you should be in bed; also the workers on duty after dark

explanation.surface: Someone rolls over in bed to watch people working in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning over' looks like rolling over in bed but is a change of position, done at night.
explanation.definitionFit: A night shift is both the group of workers on duty overnight and their overnight work period.

clue.text: Racket strings catgut, afterwards metal, for beginners

indicators.note: for beginners asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Instructions for stringing a tennis racket with catgut and then metal, aimed at novices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' looks like a tennis racket but means a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a dishonest scheme, the same as a scam.

clue.text: Dodge classes by Pearl, perhaps?

parts.note: strata are layers or classes of society
a pearl is an example of a gem

explanation.surface: Someone named Pearl teaches classes on avoiding work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pearl' looks like a person's name but is a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning trick or ploy, the same as a dodge.

clue.text: People in performance short of time? That's scary!

parts.note: men means people

indicators.note: short of means missing the named letter

parts.note: acting is performance

explanation.surface: Actors racing against the clock find it all frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short of' removes T from ACTING, leaving ACING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something menacing is threatening, which makes it frightening.

clue.text: Dash from container on craft when unoccupied on river

parts.note: a tin is a container

indicators.note: unoccupied means emptied, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Rushing from a container on an empty boat on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a rush but is a small amount. The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture is a slight trace or tinge of something, like a dash.

clue.text: Girl on unbuttressed piles gets rocket

parts.note: a miss is a girl

indicators.note: unbuttressed means the supports at each end are taken away

explanation.surface: A girl standing on unsupported heaps is given a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocket' looks like British slang for a reprimand but means a projectile.
explanation.definitionFit: A missile is a weapon propelled at a target, of which a rocket is an example.

clue.text: Make amends and leave simultaneously

parts.note: to atone is to make amends
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Apologise and walk out at the same time.
explanation.definitionFit: At one go means all together in a single action, at the same time.

clue.text: Return for spell in shed

indicators.note: return means the word is sent back the way it came, read backwards

parts.note: a spell is a period of time

explanation.surface: Coming back after a period spent in the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden building but is a verb meaning give off.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed light or heat is to emit it, to send it out.

clue.text: At all his ten late shifts …

indicators.note: shifts means the letters are moved into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Has he ever worked any of his ten late shifts? The ellipsis leads into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifts' looks like work rotas but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'in the least' means to any degree, as in 'not at all'.

clue.text: Players' union shows fairness

definitions.meaning: The British trade union for actors

explanation.surface: A sports players' union demonstrates fair dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' look like sportspeople but are actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Equity is the actors' union, and equity also means impartial fairness.

clue.text: … celebrity champion shows formality

parts.note: a celebrity is a star

explanation.surface: Following on, a famous champion behaves with stiff correctness.
explanation.definitionFit: Starch figuratively means stiffness of manner, a stiff formality.

clue.text: Son suffering quietly being purged with new energy, becoming cheerful

indicators.note: being purged means the named letters are cleaned out of the word

parts.note: anguish is severe suffering
SH is the call for quiet
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A suffering son, after a quiet purge and fresh energy, cheers up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being purged' strips SH from ANGUISH, leaving ANGUI.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanguine describes an optimistic, hopeful temperament.

clue.text: Muses maybe occasionally during Indian tea

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters, taken every other one

explanation.surface: Someone sometimes daydreams while drinking Indian tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muses' looks like a verb for daydreaming but means the Muses of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: There were nine Muses in Greek mythology, so they are an example of the number nine.

clue.text: Titchy parent's bottom?

parts.note: titchy is British slang for very small, mini
mum is a British word for mother

explanation.surface: A question about a small mother's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottom' looks like a backside but means the lowest level.
explanation.definitionFit: The minimum is the lowest possible point, the bottom of a range.

clue.text: Settling head down right among heather

indicators.note: among places one piece inside the other

parts.note: ling is another name for common heather

indicators.note: head down means the first letter is taken off

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: A bird coming to rest on the right among the heather, head lowered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head down' takes the R off RIGHT, giving IGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird lighting on a branch is alighting on it, coming down to settle.

clue.text: Roll unwrapped Easter egg at Scottish reel

indicators.note: to roll something over turns it round, so the letters run backwards
unwrapped shows letters revealed inside the words when the outer parts are removed

explanation.surface: Rolling an Easter egg along during a Scottish dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unwrapped' finds REGGATS inside 'EasteR EGG AT Scottish'; 'Roll' turns it round. 'reel' looks like the dance but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to stagger, to walk unsteadily as if about to fall.
